A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BlueSuffix and retain matching methods and experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original jailbreak-defense experiments, component ablations, benign-prompt evaluations, transfer tests, and an adaptive-attack evaluation.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds attack/model comparisons, a suffix-only ablation, mutual-information estimates, semantic-similarity scores, and toxicity evaluations.

M1.justification: The diffusion image purifier, LLM text purifier, PPO-trained GPT-2 suffix generator, reward objective, and inference pipeline remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. Renaming the suffix variable does not change the method. The revised training-data description is an experimental-setting change.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluations on AdvBench and Harmful Instructions alongside the retained MM-SafetyBench, RedTeam-2K, and AlpacaEval coverage. It also adds visual attacks VAA and imgJP and textual attacks GCG and AutoDAN, substantially extending the tested input conditions beyond vanilla and BAP attacks.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds R2D2 and CAT comparisons on open-source models and VLGuard on LLaVA, including within the retained BAP experiment. DiffPure, Safety Prompt, and their combination remain; the table's System Prompt label refers to the retained Safety Prompt comparator. Jailguard and CIDER are not evaluated in either version.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated suffix-generator training data from MM-SafetyBench's financial-advice topic to all 13 topics; the PDFs do not establish whether shared experiments were rerun. v2 adds InstructionBLIP target/source configurations, 100-prompt AdvBench evaluations, and 40-prompt Harmful Instructions evaluations. New analyses introduce 50 selected prompt pairs with four input configurations for mutual information, semantic scoring, and Perspective toxicity scoring.

E4.justification: v2 adds a suffix-generator-only ablation, a cross-modal utilization analysis in Section 4.3, semantic-preservation testing in Appendix B, and an alternative toxicity assessment in Appendix H. It removes the detailed per-topic component-ablation tables from v1 Appendix E while retaining their aggregate results. The adaptive-attack test and existing illustrative cases remain.

E5.justification: v2 Section 4.3 introduces a statistical estimation procedure: k-nearest-neighbor estimation of mutual information from 50 prompt pairs. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results, including 0.00% BlueSuffix ASR for the new visual/textual attack evaluations, 6.78% against BAP on InstructionBLIP, suffix-only ablation scores, and semantic-similarity averages of 4.82 and 4.87. Shared BAP averages, benign-prompt scores, purifier comparisons, and adaptive-attack values remain numerically unchanged. Numerous per-topic baseline, attack, and ablation entries from v1 Tables 1, 4, 6, and 7 disappear.

T1.justification: The black-box and one-shot threat assumptions, problem formulation, and equations 1–7 are retained. The suffix-symbol change is not substantive mathematics. The new mutual-information analysis reports empirical estimates without adding a formal definition, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The first contribution shifts emphasis from defending universal adversarial visual triggers to a generic, extensible, plug-and-play framework, explicitly claiming integration and extension of existing techniques. The central defense, benign-utility, transferability, and approximately 70%/50% ASR-reduction claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations that purification assists suffix-generator fine-tuning and that training the generator without purifiers can harm benign utility. Appendix H specifically qualifies Perspective toxicity scoring as potentially unsuitable for judging jailbreaks. Some category-specific vulnerability interpretations from v1 are removed, while the rewriting-failure example and future-adaptive-attack caveat remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code link, an explicit judge prompt, further attack/baseline descriptions, and the CFFF computing-platform acknowledgment. The rewrite template and core PPO settings remain unchanged. The new judge template assigns 1 to harmful responses, opposite to the retained benign=1 reward convention, without explaining the conversion; its disclosure does not establish an implementation change.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for AutoDAN, HarmBench/R2D2, CAT, VLGuard, PPO, and DeepSeek-VL2, and expands comparison with adversarial-training defenses. The related-work taxonomy and positioning against Jailguard/CIDER largely remain. Most other bibliography changes update publication metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution wording, and portions of the experimental exposition are edited; attack descriptions become a separate setup paragraph, and the appendices are reorganized. Author/correspondence information and acknowledgments also change. Much of the introduction, method, transferability discussion, and conclusion remains closely matched, so the editorial revision is limited.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned from per-topic BAP blocks into an attack-by-model comparison, a mutual-information table is added, and v1 Tables 4, 6, and 7 are removed. Figure 3 gains a suffix-only series, the transfer table expands, and a judge-template figure is added. Existing illustrations are retained but relocated or resized, including v1 Figure 4 becoming v2 Figure 7 in Appendix I.

improvement.justification: The broader attack and defense comparisons in v2 Table 1 address v1's narrow empirical support for generality, while the suffix-only control and additional evaluation documentation improve assessability. These gains are tempered by removal of detailed topic-level evidence and an unexplained training-description change from one topic to all 13 despite unchanged shared scores. The net improvement is supported but limited.
